array_slice() resets numeric keys by default, so it does not preserve the original numeric keys unless you pass true as the fourth argument.

The union operator (+) combines arrays keeping the left-hand side's values for duplicate keys, resulting in ['a' => 1, 'b' => 2].

In PHP, boolean array keys are automatically converted to integers (true becomes 1, false becomes 0) rather than being stored as booleans.
A generator's return statement can include a value, and since PHP 7.1 this return value is retrievable via the Generator::getReturn() method after the generator is closed.

The generator yields 3 elements from the array [1, 2, 3], so count() will return 3.
The SplStack class implements a LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) stack using push() and pop(), whereas the SplDoublyLinkedList implements a FIFO queue.

ArrayObject implements Traversable and Iterator, so it can be fully traversed with foreach.

Property hooks (get/set in the property declaration) were indeed introduced in PHP 8.4.

The pipe operator (|>) was introduced in PHP 8.1 as of January 2022.

In Symfony, services are not created lazily by default; the container factory creates all services eagerly when the container is compiled/loaded, and only services explicitly marked as lazy-loading proxies (via the 'lazy' attribute or as autowired async services) are instantiated on first use.

Symfony autowiring automatically wires services based on type hints without manual declaration, so you don't need to manually declare every service in services.yaml.
Twig compiles templates into optimized PHP classes and caches them on disk (in the cache directory) between requests for performance.

In the Symfony dev environment, the container cache is only rebuilt when tracked configuration or source files change, which is optimized via the ConfigCache that checks file mtimes before invalidating.
In modern Symfony applications the active environment is selected via the APP_ENV variable (typically set in the .env file), while older versions used the SYMFY_ENV variable.
In Symfony, controller methods referenced in routes must be public, as private or protected methods cannot be invoked through the normal request handling mechanism.

Event subscribers and listeners are dispatched based on their priority (via the getSubscribedEvents priority option or the addEventListener priority argument), not because subscribing is inherently higher-priority than listening.
Symfony 6.0+ uses the modern authenticator-based system and removed the old guard system, which was deprecated in Symfony 5.9 and eliminated in 6.0.
The IsGranted attribute (or @IsGranted annotation) checks a role or permission on a controller method and returns HTTP 403 when the check fails.

Symfony forms enable CSRF protection by default by including and validating a hidden _token field on submission.

The `make:form` command in Symfony's MakerBundle generates a form class (FormType).
Symfony never stores passwords in the session; passwords are hashed when stored in the user provider, and the session only holds a user identifier/reference, never the password itself.
Symfony bundles are configured via YAML/XML files in config/packages, with one file per bundle or topic.
This matches Symfony's .env convention where .env contains committed dev defaults and .env.local holds local secrets that git-ignores.
The `debug:container` command displays all registered services in the Symfony container, including their aliases when the --show-aliases option is used.

Bundles work perfectly without configuration files because they provide default values through their Extension class's load() method, making configuration entirely optional.
Environment variables are injected using the %env(VAR)% syntax, but the statement is false because the %env() parameter syntax must be wrapped in quotes (e.g., "%env(VAR)%") in services.yaml.
The APP_DEBUG environment variable, when set to "1", enables debug mode in Symfony which activates the profiler and Twig's debugging capabilities.
A single message in Symfony Messenger can be handled by multiple handlers, as handlers are configured by message type and any number of handlers can be registered for the same message.

Symfony Scheduler, introduced in Symfony 7.2, triggers closures directly on a schedule and does not integrate with the Messenger component to dispatch messages.
